title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. AI-generated video was used to depict a real person saying things she never said, and the output was published to a social platform under the poster's own account. The false statements were attributed to a named individual, which is what makes the material a deepfake rather than satire or parody, and the distribution channel was a public feed rather than a closed or labelled context.

Catching this kind of content requires knowing what the depicted person actually said. The claim that the statements were never made comes from the subject's attorneys, and the videos themselves carry no marker of being synthetic. A platform check, a press query to the person depicted, or a viewer who already knew her positions could have surfaced the mismatch, but none of those steps sits inside the posting workflow.

What is not established is whether the videos violated any law. A cease-and-desist letter is a demand, not a ruling, and the defamation claim it raises has not been tested in court.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Prairie du Chien, over his use of AI-generated deepfake videos. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District. Van Orden has posted videos to X showing fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip shared on Aug. 4. The letter, dated Sept. 30, says Cooke never made those statements and accuses Van Orden of trying to fool voters and harm her reputation.

The letter warns that Van Orden could violate state defamation law and says Cooke's attorneys are monitoring his social media accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum. Cooke lost to Van Orden in 2024 by about 3 percentage points. Van Orden responded this week with another AI-assisted video featuring a red duck saying "Cease and desist!"
